newsitem.title: UK: Unilever to sell chemicals units.
newsitem.headline: Unilever to sell chemicals units.

text.p: Unilever Plc/NV said on Tuesday it intends to sell its international speciality chemicals businesses.
These comprise National Starch and Chemical Co, Quest International, Unichema International and Crosfield, the Anglo-Dutch consumer goods company said in a statement.

Chairman Niall Fitzgerald said sale of the speciality chemicals businesses would enable Unilever to "concentrate resources on achieving superior long-term growth in our consumer goods operations, particularly in developing and emerging markets."
No figure was given for the amount likely to be raised from the sale.

"This industry is currently undergoing considerable realignment and a sale of our businesses at this time would allow them to participate more fully in the opportunities that this re-alignment presents," Fitzgerald said in a statement with Unilever's 1996 results.
The operations to be sold had combined turnover, including sales to other Unilever companies, of some three billion stg in 1996, representing nine percent of Unilever's total sales.
They employ some 15,800 people in more than 35 countries.
National Starch and Chemical Co is a worldwide producer of industrial adhesives, resins and speciality chemicals headquartered in the U.S.
Quest International, based in the Netherlands, makes fragrances as well as food flavour and ingredients.

Unichema International, also based in the Netherlands, is involved in speciality oleochemicals and nickel catalysts, while Crosfield, and international producer of inorganic chemicals based on silica and alumina, is headquartered in Britain.
Unilever has appointed Lazard Bros and Lazard Freres and Co to advise on and conduct the sale process, and further announcements will be made as appropriate.
